input.rationale: Customer is locked into a minimum monthly fee (Monthly Base Fee) payable in advance (p0149) for an eight-year Term (p0049), and can exit only by paying a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value measured off that minimum (p0039). That is a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction right and no true-up, so every fallback element fails. Because deleting the minimum outright would require collateral rewrites to the payment, bundling and termination-fee machinery, we target the fallback with one new Section 8.1A capping the commitment at the then-current twelve-month period, permitting reduction on thirty days' notice and trueing up any shortfall with no penalty. Section 10.3.A is made subject to that reduction right only (its "during the Term" sourcing period is left untouched, as shortening it would be an exclusivity concession outside this checklist). Noted but not flagged here: the Estimated Remaining Value formula still runs to the eighth anniversary, which is a termination-fee issue for the termination rule.

mappings.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.

proposal.summary: Limit the Monthly Base Fee minimum commitment to the current 12-month period, allow reduction on 30 days' notice, and true-up any shortfall instead of a penalty.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot take an eight-year take-or-pay minimum, so we limited the minimum monthly fee commitment to the then-current twelve-month period, added a 30 days' notice reduction right, and replaced any shortfall charge with a true-up, with Section 10.3.A made subject to that reduction right. Our preferred position is no minimum commitment at all, but this fallback is acceptable.

ops.text: 8.1A Minimum Commitment. Customer's minimum monthly fee commitment (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term, and Customer may reduce such commitment upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I. If Customer's actual usage-based charges for such period are less than the committed amount, Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up, and no penalty or shortfall charge shall apply.
